newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products mostly lower with soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products mostly lower with soybeans.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures were mostly lower at midsession Monday, primarily in response to losses in old crop soybeans, traders said.
July soybeans fell sharply Monday as traders took profits on the July/November spread.
In export business, South Korea re-invited tenders for 40,000 tonnes of soymeal. However, CBOT traders said that business was destined for South American exporters.
Activity in the soyoil trading pit was quiet. There has been very little export business in the past several months, and cash markets have also been lackluster, traders said.
"The oil market is a real dog right now," said one soyoil trader.
In early trading, commission houses were light sellers of soyoil while commercial houses were buyers. ADM bought 200 lots July and Cargill bought 150 December, pit sources said.
In soymeal trade, ADM sold 300 lots July, Merrill Lynch sold 300 July and Refco sold 200 July, 100 August and 100 December, pit sources said.
At 1219 CDT, soyoil was down 0.01 to 0.02 cent per lb, with July down 0.02 at 23.76. Soymeal futures were $1.50 per tonne lower to $4.50 higher, with July down $4.50 at $286.00.
